L01.note: two adjacent pairs 10/11 and 13/14, nothing distinguishes either pair

L02.note: 6 and 20 are primitives, 120 is their product and 26 their sum; a sum is the usual ask when both parts are offered

L03.note: 12.5 is the hub: half of 25 and 5 more than 7.5, while 25 and 5 are the round primitives

L04.note: every other option is a clean multiple of 225 (x1.25, x0.8, x4/3), so 225 is the derivational hub

L05.note: 190/200/210 form an arithmetic run with 130 as an outlier; the centre of a +/-10 run is usually the key

L06.note: 48/32 and 42/28 both sit at ratio 1.5, which identifies the structure but not which member is the key

L07.note: 6.36 is an order-of-magnitude outlier and 2.04/2.28 are a near-miss pair, but the pick inside that pair is a coin flip

L08.note: 1 and 9 read as roots with 10 their sum and 5 their mean; sum of solutions is the commonest ask

L09.note: 80 generates the rest (x0.75 = 60, x0.3 = 24) so it is the hub of the ratio chain

L10.note: 65/85 and 70/80 are both symmetric about 75; no asymmetry to exploit

L11.note: 73 is the only non-round value among 64, 100 and 88, and squares make natural distractors

L12.note: 2025 is the only non-round value; 2160, 1800 and 2700 are round ratio-errors around it

L13.note: 21 divided by 4 is exactly 5.25 and both 21 and 4 are present as distractors

L14.note: 23 is the odd prime against 12, 20 and 15; weakest form of the non-round tell

L15.note: 260 = 400 - 140 exactly, and 4 is a magnitude outlier, so 260 is the combination the others are parts of

L16.note: 15,16,18,19 are symmetric about the absent 17; no signal

L17.note: 386/402/428/446 have no clean ratio or difference structure

L18.note: 90 is exactly twice 45, the classic forgot-to-halve distractor, which points at 45

L19.note: 4/5 and -4/5 are a sign pair; a negative slope from standard form is the likelier key

L20.note: (9,6) and (8,5) both differ by 3; no way to choose a member

L22.note: 26250 is the only non-round value among three round thousands

L23.note: 5/-5 sign pair with 3 and 9=3^2 alongside; structure visible but the key is not

L24.note: 210 and 270 generate both 480 (sum) and 60 (difference), so the key is one of the generators; 270 chosen within the pair

L25.note: 10 is the harmonic mean of 6 and 30, the signature of a round-trip rate answer

L26.note: 20, 30, 45 is a geometric chain at ratio 1.5; the centre is where multiply/divide errors land on the ends

L27.note: -9,-8,-6,-5 symmetric about the absent -7; no signal

L28.note: -1 is the sign outlier but 2, 3, 4 are indistinguishable
